2027-01-06.title: Denha · The Epiphany and Baptism of our Lord
2027-01-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: A star shall come out of Jacob
The spirit of the Lord shall rest on him
The water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
This is my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-06.alt: Important feast and day of obligation. The Third Qudasha (anaphora) is used in the Holy Qurbana. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
2027-01-06.verse: And a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”
theo: Denha is a Syriac word meaning dawn, rising, manifestation. The Eastern Churches celebrate on this day not first the Magi but the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God shone out: the Son in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.” At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed, and the public ministry of Jesus begins. The Sun of Justice rises over the world.

The readings show a dawn long promised. The seer Balaam, a stranger to Israel, looks out from the hills of Moab and sees far ahead: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near”, and he announces that “a star shall come out of Jacob”. Isaiah sees a shoot from the stump of Jesse and promises: “The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might”. At the Jordan both promises meet. The star has risen, and the Spirit comes down and rests on Jesus, as Matthew says: “he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him.”

John protests: “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” Jesus had no sin. Yet he answers that “it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness”: he goes down into the water to stand with sinners and to sanctify the waters for us. St Paul tells Titus what this means for us: God “saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit. This Spirit he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior”. Our ancestors' customs, the lamps on plantain stems with the cry El Paiya, God is light, and the night bath recalling the Jordan, were ways of saying: our Baptism has made us children of light. Denha calls each of us to remember our Baptism and to live as beloved sons and daughters.
conn: Syriac for dawn or rising. The feast is called Denha (Epiphany) in the East Syriac tradition, and in Kerala popularly Pindikuthi in the north and Rakkuli in the south.
Lamps were fixed on a plantain stem (pindi) and the family processed around it crying “El Paiya”, a Syriac-Malayalam cry meaning God is light. Christ is the light of the world.
On the eve, families bathed in rivers or ponds at night (rakkuli, “night bath”), recalling the Jordan. It was a religious act of remembering Baptism, not a magical rite.

Balaam, a seer from outside Israel, foretells a star and a sceptre (Numbers 24:17). Many Fathers linked this star with the star of the Magi; the East Syriac tradition keeps the whole manifestation of Christ in this one feast.

Only Matthew records John's protest and Jesus' reply (Matthew 3:14–15). Jesus takes his place among sinners, as the Servant who will bear their sins, and so begins the obedience that leads to the Cross.
In many Eastern Churches water is solemnly blessed at Denha, because Christ sanctified the waters by his baptism (CCC 1224).

On the Fridays of this season the Church remembers the great witnesses of Christ: John the Baptist, Peter and Paul, the Evangelists, Stephen, the Greek and Syrian Fathers, and finally all the faithful departed.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today, with its rich prayers on the Holy Trinity. At the Jordan the Trinity was revealed; at the altar the Trinity gives us the Body and Blood of the Son by the Spirit.
In Baptism we went down into the water with Christ; in the Holy Qurbana we are fed as beloved children.

2027-01-06.prayer: O Christ, Sun of Justice, today you rose upon the world at the Jordan. The Father bore witness to you, and the Spirit of wisdom came down and rested on you. Sanctify us who were washed in the water of rebirth; pour out your Spirit richly upon us; and let us live as beloved children of light. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise and glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

family.explain: Jesus came to the river Jordan and asked John to baptise him. When he came up out of the water, heaven opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God the Father said: this is my Son, I love him!
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptised this year.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised? Let us find out.”

illus: A family in Changanassery keeps a small book with the baptismal date of each child. On that date there is no party, but a candle is lit at dinner and the child renews the baptismal promises. The children say it is their favourite day of the year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this feast of Denha you went down into the Jordan and the heavens were opened. Open heaven over us as we gather, and pour out your Spirit. Amen.
share: A star shall come out of Jacob (Numbers 24:17). How has Christ become light for me?
This is my Son, the Beloved (Matthew 3:17). Do I believe that God looks on me with the same love?
He saved us through the water of rebirth (Titus 3:5). How do I live my Baptism day by day?
pm.resp: Christ, our Light, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may shine with the light of the Holy Trinity.
For all baptised Christians, that they may live as children of light.
For catechumens and those preparing for Baptism.
For those who have abandoned the faith received in Baptism.
For our group, that the Spirit may renew God's gifts in us.
pm.close: Father, at the Jordan you declared Jesus your beloved Son, and your Spirit rested on him. Keep us faithful to our Baptism, and make our lives shine with your light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed feast of Denha to you. Denha means dawn, rising, manifestation. Our Church celebrates today the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God was revealed.

Look at the scene in Matthew. Jesus comes from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptised. John tries to stop him: I need to be baptised by you, and do you come to me? Jesus answers: let it be so now; it is proper for us in this way to fulfil all righteousness (Matthew 3:14–15). The sinless one takes his place in the line of sinners.

And when he comes up from the water, the heavens are opened, the Spirit of God descends like a dove and alights on him, and a voice from heaven says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:16–17). Son, Spirit and Father: the Holy Trinity is revealed.

Long before, Balaam had seen from afar: a star shall come out of Jacob (Numbers 24:17). Isaiah had promised a shoot from the stump of Jesse on whom the spirit of the Lord would rest, the spirit of wisdom and understanding (Isaiah 11:1–2). At the Jordan the star rises and the Spirit rests. The dawn has come.

Our ancestors kept this feast beautifully. They lit lamps on plantain stems and walked around crying El Paiya, God is light. On the eve they bathed in rivers and ponds, remembering the Jordan. These customs said: we are baptised; we are children of light.

St Paul tells Titus that God saved us, not because of works we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit, poured out on us richly (Titus 3:5–6). Many of us were baptised as infants and rarely think of it. Today, let us remember: God has said to you, you are my beloved son, my beloved daughter. Let us live as people who have heard that voice. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Denha! Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God said: this is my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said the same about you: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents when your Baptism day is!

homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Holy Qurbana as children of an open heaven. Amen.

intro: Most of us were baptised as infants and remember nothing. Today the Church asks us to remember what God did.

sub: The candle lit from the Easter flame.

concl: Baptism is not only a past event but a present identity.
We live as children of God, clothed with Christ, walking in the light.
opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Holy Qurbana as children of the light. Amen.
